claim: The southern extremity, where the Cote d'Or gives way to the Cote Chalonnaise
because: Santenay is not the southern extremity of the Cote de Beaune. Maranges (Cheilly-, Dezize- and Sampigny-les-Maranges, its own village AOC since 1989) lies south-west of Santenay and is the southernmost appellation of the Cote de Beaune. Louis Latour and burgundywine.com both give Maranges as the southern tip. The keyed answer, the southern end, still stands.
fix: Toward the southern tip, with only Maranges beyond it before the Cote d'Or gives way to the Cote Chalonnaise, and traditionally a source of value.
